C2. Data Coverage(heatmap)

# read_hh 
def read_hh(zip_file: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    parts = zip_file.stem.split("_")
    site = parts[1]
    years = parts[3]

    keep = ["TIMESTAMP_START", "TIMESTAMP_END", "TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F",
            "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC",
            "NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF_QC", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF"]

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_file) as z, z.open(
        next(n for n in z.namelist() if "FLUXNET_FLUXMET_HH" in n)
    ) as f:
        hh = pd.read_csv(f, na_values=[-9999],
                         usecols=lambda c: c in keep,
                         dtype={"TIMESTAMP_START": str, "TIMESTAMP_END": str})

    hh["time"] = pd.to_datetime(hh["TIMESTAMP_START"], format="%Y%m%d%H%M")   
    hh["site"] = site  

    y_start, y_end = map(int, years.split("-"))
    t_min, t_max = hh["time"].min(), hh["time"].max()
    assert t_min.year == y_start, f"{site}: start year not same ({t_min.year} != {y_start})"
    assert t_max.year == y_end,   f"{site}: end year not same ({t_max.year} != {y_end})"
    assert not hh["time"].duplicated().any(), f"{site}: duplicate timestamps exist"

    n_by_year = hh.groupby(hh["time"].dt.year).size()
    bad = n_by_year[(n_by_year != 17520) & (n_by_year != 17568)]
    if len(bad):
        print(f"⚠ {site}: the year row number ist different:\n{bad}")

    return hh[["site", "time"] +
              [c for c in keep if c not in ("TIMESTAMP_START", "TIMESTAMP_END")]]

C3. Summary statistics

# ── 1. variables ────────────────
units = {
    'TA_F':            '°C',
    'SW_IN_F':         'W m⁻²',
    'VPD_F':           'hPa',
    'P_F':             'mm yr⁻¹',   
    'NEE_VUT_REF':     'µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹',
    'GPP_NT_VUT_REF':  'µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹',
    'RECO_NT_VUT_REF': 'µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹',
    'H_F_MDS':         'W m⁻²',
    'LE_F_MDS':        'W m⁻²',
}

stat_vars = list(units.keys())
all_hh['year'] = all_hh['time'].dt.year   

# ── 2. table by each site ─────────────────────────────
site_tables = {}

for site, g in all_hh.groupby('site'):
    rows = []
    for var in stat_vars:
        s = g[var]

        if var == 'P_F':
            annual_sum = g.groupby('year')['P_F'].sum(min_count=1)
            mean_val = annual_sum.mean()
        else:
            mean_val = s.mean()

        rows.append({
            'Variable': f"{var} ({units[var]})",
            'Mean':     mean_val,
            'Min':      s.min(),
            'Max':      s.max(),
            '% Missing': s.isna().mean() * 100,
        })

    site_tables[site] = pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2)
    display(site_tables[site].style.hide(axis='index')
            .set_caption(f"Site: {site}"))

C5. Diurnal Cycle

# ── 1. southern hemisphere ──────────────────
lat_map = (snapshot[['site_id', 'location_lat']]
           .drop_duplicates()
           .set_index('site_id')['location_lat'])

# ── 2. weather column  ────────────────
season_of_month = {12:'DJF', 1:'DJF', 2:'DJF',
                   3:'MAM', 4:'MAM', 5:'MAM',
                   6:'JJA', 7:'JJA', 8:'JJA',
                   9:'SON', 10:'SON', 11:'SON'}

def get_season(month, lat):
    if lat < 0:
        month = (month + 5) % 12 + 1   # for southern
    return season_of_month[month]

all_hh['month'] = all_hh['time'].dt.month
all_hh['hour']  = all_hh['time'].dt.hour + all_hh['time'].dt.minute / 60  # 0.0~23.5
all_hh['season'] = [get_season(m, lat_map[s]) for m, s in zip(all_hh['month'], all_hh['site'])]

# ── 3. sites × weather × time ─────────────────────────────
cycle = (all_hh
         .groupby(['site', 'season', 'hour'])[['NEE_VUT_REF', 'LE_F_MDS']]
         .mean()
         .reset_index())

print(cycle.head(3))
print("\n weather by sites:")
print(all_hh.groupby('site')['season'].value_counts().unstack())

C6. Your reading

# ── 1. fing sites ──────────────────────────
avail = all_hh.groupby('site')[['NETRAD', 'G_F_MDS']].apply(
    lambda g: g.notna().mean()
)
print("percentage of not missing:")
print(avail.round(3))

# available sites
ok_sites = avail[(avail['NETRAD'] > 0.5) & (avail['G_F_MDS'] > 0.5)].index.tolist()
print("\navailable sites:", ok_sites)

eb_site = 'US-MOz'

# ── 2. H, LE (QC==0) use only half hourly ────────────────────
eb = all_hh[
    (all_hh['site'] == eb_site) &
    (all_hh['H_F_MDS_QC'] == 0) &
    (all_hh['LE_F_MDS_QC'] == 0) &
    all_hh['NETRAD'].notna() &      
    all_hh['G_F_MDS'].notna()       
].copy()

x = eb['NETRAD'] - eb['G_F_MDS']   # available energy
y = eb['H_F_MDS'] + eb['LE_F_MDS'] # used energy

# ── 3. slope of OLs ────────────────────────────────────────
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
print(f"\n{eb_site}: slope = {slope:.3f}, intercept = {intercept:.2f}, n = {len(eb)}")

# ── 4. scatterplot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))

ax.scatter(x, y, s=2, alpha=0.15, color='tab:blue')
lims = [min(x.min(), y.min()), max(x.max(), y.max())]
ax.plot(lims, lims, 'k--', lw=1, label='1:1 line')                  # 1:1 
ax.plot(lims, slope*np.array(lims)+intercept, 'r-', lw=1.5,
        label=f'fit: slope = {slope:.2f}')

ax.set_xlabel('NETRAD − G_F_MDS (W m⁻²)')
ax.set_ylabel('H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS (W m⁻²)')
ax.set_title(f'Energy Balance Closure — {eb_site}')
ax.legend()
ax.set_aspect('equal')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

  1. Site Comparison 1-1. CH-Fru, IT-BCi, JP-SMF, and US-MOz At these four sites, NEE reaches its lowest values around midday and NEE values are also generally lower in JJA (summer) than in other seasons. Similarly, LE (latent heat flux) reaches its highest values around midday due to sufficient sunlight and higher temperatures, with the highest evaporation activity occurring during JJA. 2 1-2. IL-Yat (semi-Mediterranean , dry region) From March to August, LE decreases due to water limitation and NEE increases as plants reduce photosynthesis to minimize water loss. Plants also tend to avoid midday, resulting in two distinct daily NEE peaks outside midday. 2
  2. Energy Balance Closure Problem (US-MOz, Tall Forest) The energy balance closure ratio at US-MOz is approximately 0.639, meaning that turbulent fluxes account for only about 63.9% of the available energy measured by NETRAD. (US-MOz site has the lowest gap-filled data for H, LE, each for 87.6,79.6 measured proportion)

Data and citation

Data

The site metadata were taken from the FLUXNET Shuttle snapshot data/snapshots/fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261113T113806.csv. Half-hourly (FLUXNET_FLUXMET_HH) and daily (FLUXNET_FLUXMET_DD) data products were downloaded as zip archives (e.g. AMF_US-MOz_FLUXNET_FLUXMET_HH_2004-2021_v1.3_r1.zip), all with product version ONEFlux v1.3, release r1 (2026 release).

Site citations

**US-MOz** (Missouri Ozark Site, US): Jeffrey Wood, Lianhong Gu (2026), AmeriFlux FLUXNET-1F US-MOz Missouri Ozark Site, Ver. v1.3_r1 (2004-2021), AmeriFlux AMP, (Dataset). https://doi.org/10.17190/AMF/1854370
**JP-SMF** (Seto Mixed Forest Site, JP): Kotani, A., Ohta, T., Ohta, T. (2026). Fluxnet Archive Product from Seto Mixed Forest Site, 2002–2014, FLUXNET, https://hdl.handle.net/11676/OJmZUckooZnjzhPVMCBvUM85
**IT-BCi** (Borgo Cioffi, IT): Magliulo, V., Calandrelli, D., Cuocolo, D., Di Tommasi, P., Esposito, A., Famulari, D., Manco, A., Vitale, L., Zenone, T., Zenone, T. (2026). Fluxnet Archive Product from Borgo Cioffi, 2004-01-01–2026-09-06, FLUXNET, https://hdl.handle.net/11676/QcwmmUDyX5MXPIYAuDq5vepJ
**IL-Yat** (Yatir, IL): Rotenberg, E., Schwartz, E., Yakir, D. (2026). Fluxnet Archive Product from Yatir, 2000–2024, FLUXNET, https://hdl.handle.net/11676/ddBS_ZLjXuBI8SSQV2cskqda
**CH-Fru** (Fruebuel, CH): Buchmann, N., Hortnagl, L., Zeeman, M., Merbold, L., Merbold, L., Fuchs, K., Feigenwinter, I., Burri, S., Baur, T., Meier, P. (2025). Fluxnet Archive Product from Fruebuel, 2005–2024, FLUXNET, https://hdl.handle.net/11676/xnRKIWdx6isC5GLqv_pHq5hU
